title: Taxpayer Experience Improvement Act

claims.claim: The bill requires the IRS to publish real-time data on its public website.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary shall require the Internal Revenue Service to provide in real time on its public website

claims.claim: Real-time data covers phone wait times and call volumes.
claims.sourceSpan: the longest amount of time that any caller has been waiting to be connected to speak directly with a representative of the Internal Revenue Service,
claims.note: Call volumes = 2(a)(1)(A)-(C) caller counts; wait time = 2(a)(1)(D).

claims.claim: Real-time data covers processing backlogs for every public phone line it operates.
claims.sourceSpan: during the week subsequent to the applicable week
claims.note: Two imprecisions: (1) delay/backlog info is published the SUBSEQUENT week, not in real time; (2) backlog info attaches to 'applicable items' (document categories per 2(d)(1)), not to phone lines. Also 'every public phone line it operates' overstates the narrow 'applicable phone number extension' definition (2(d)(2)). Gloss, non-material.

claims.claim: The data is made available through a public API so third-party apps can display it.
claims.sourceSpan: An application programming interface which allows any person to access the information described in subsection (a)(1) using automation

claims.claim: The bill gives taxpayers online or mobile access to their own tax returns and notices.
claims.sourceSpan: view any return (as defined in section 6103(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986), document, notice, or letter
claims.note: Viewing of returns/notices is Section 5 (online accounts), not Section 3; synthesis field may draw on any registered source.

claims.claim: The bill gives taxpayers refund status including an estimated delivery date.
claims.sourceSpan: the estimated date on which the taxpayer can expect to receive such refund

claims.claim: Requires the IRS to publish live phone wait times and backlog data.
claims.sourceSpan: Establishment of dashboard to inform taxpayers of backlogs and wait times

claims.claim: Gives taxpayers digital access to their own returns and refund status.
claims.sourceSpan: through a website and mobile application, the Secretary shall provide individualized, specific, and up-to-date information to taxpayers regarding their tax returns and amended returns

claims.claim: Real-Time IRS Dashboard.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary shall require the Internal Revenue Service to provide in real time on its public website

claims.claim: IRS must publish live caller counts, wait times, and callback availability per phone line on its public website.
claims.sourceSpan: whether callback service is currently available, and if not, when such service is scheduled to be available.
claims.note: Caller counts 2(a)(1)(A)-(C); wait time 2(a)(1)(D); callback availability 2(a)(1)(E); 'per phone line' = per applicable phone number extension.

claims.claim: Public API required so any person or app can access the live call data.
claims.sourceSpan: An application programming interface which allows any person to access the information described in subsection (a)(1) using automation

claims.claim: This top line binds to bill Section 2.
claims.sourceSpan: Establishment of dashboard to inform taxpayers of backlogs and wait times
claims.note: billSection '2' correctly matches dashboard/API content.

claims.claim: Digital Tax Record Access.
claims.sourceSpan: view any return (as defined in section 6103(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986), document, notice, or letter

claims.claim: Taxpayers can view all returns, notices, and IRS letters via website or mobile app.
claims.sourceSpan: view any return (as defined in section 6103(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986), document, notice, or letter
claims.note: Capability is real but lives in Section 5 (online accounts), while this top line is tagged billSection '3'. Also 'all' drops the preceding-6-year-period limit (5(d)(1)) and the educational-item exception. Minor.

claims.claim: IRS must provide estimated refund receipt date.
claims.sourceSpan: the estimated date on which the taxpayer can expect to receive such refund
claims.note: This sub correctly belongs to Section 3, matching billSection '3'.

claims.claim: Monthly Accountability Metrics.
claims.sourceSpan: a summary of the information described in paragraph (1) with respect to the prior month

claims.claim: IRS must publish monthly averages for call length, hold time, disconnection rate, and percent of callers who got help.
claims.sourceSpan: the number and percent of callers who indicated that they received the answers or service for which they were contacting the Internal Revenue Service.
claims.note: Call length 2(a)(4)(A); hold time 2(a)(4)(F); disconnection 2(a)(4)(D); percent got help 2(a)(4)(G). All Section 2 content, but the top line is tagged billSection '3'.

claims.claim: Sense of Congress: callback offered within 5 minutes on any unanswered call by 2028.
claims.sourceSpan: not later than calendar year 2028, the Internal Revenue Service should provide any taxpayer (including any taxpayer residing outside of the United States) the option to receive a callback for any call made by the taxpayer to an applicable phone number extension (as defined in section 2(d)(2) of this Act) which has not been answered within 5 minutes.
claims.note: Section 4 content, but the top line is tagged billSection '3'.

claims.claim: This top line (monthly metrics + callback sense-of-Congress) binds to bill Section 3.
claims.sourceSpan: a summary of the information described in paragraph (1) with respect to the prior month
claims.note: billSection '3' is wrong: the monthly metrics are Section 2(a)(4) and the callback sense-of-Congress is Section 4. Section 3 (returns/refunds) contains neither. A reader following the section anchor lands in the wrong provision. Best single anchor = '2'.

claims.claim: Only 1 cosponsor.
claims.sourceSpan: Mr. Schweikert (for himself and Mr. Beyer )
claims.note: One cosponsor (Beyer) shown in the introduction line; cosponsor count is structural metadata.

claims.claim: Bipartisan sponsorship (Schweikert R-AZ and Beyer D-VA).
claims.sourceSpan: Mr. Schweikert (for himself and Mr. Beyer )
claims.note: Beyer as cosponsor is sourced; party/state are structural member-roster facts (allowed under framing class); 'bipartisan' = R sponsor + D cosponsor, structural.

claims.claim: IRS modernization bills often pass the House but stall in the Senate amid disagreements over IRS funding and IT capacity.
claims.sourceSpan: To provide for modernization and technological improvements of services provided by the Internal Revenue Service.
claims.note: Extrinsic legislative-prognosis commentary, not in source. Presented as prediction rather than fact; non-material.

claims.claim: The real-time dashboard and public API requirements may face resistance from the Treasury Department over implementation feasibility.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary shall require the Internal Revenue Service to provide in real time on its public website
claims.note: Dashboard/API requirements are sourced; the 'may face resistance' prediction is extrinsic and hedged. Non-material.

claims.claim: Names the Act the Taxpayer Experience Improvement Act, defines Secretary as the Secretary of the Treasury or delegate, and lists the table of contents.
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the Taxpayer Experience Improvement Act
claims.note: Secretary def at 1(b); table of contents at 1(c).

claims.claim: Short-title/definitions/table-of-contents section with no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: the term Secretary means the Secretary of the Treasury

claims.claim: Requires the IRS to publish in real time on its public website call volume, wait time, and callback availability for each applicable phone number extension.
claims.sourceSpan: Separately with respect to each applicable phone number extension

claims.claim: For each phone line, the IRS must display callers connected to representatives, to automated systems, and waiting; the longest current wait time; and whether callback service is available.
claims.sourceSpan: the number of callers connected to speak directly with a representative of the Internal Revenue Service,

claims.claim: A public API must be provided for automated access to the data.
claims.sourceSpan: An application programming interface which allows any person to access the information described in subsection (a)(1) using automation

claims.claim: The IRS must also detect and screen automated calls.
claims.sourceSpan: use technology to detect and screen out automated calls

claims.claim: The IRS must publish processing delay information weekly when significant backlogs occur.
claims.sourceSpan: For any week in which there was a significant delay with respect to any applicable item
claims.note: Published during the subsequent week; 'weekly when significant backlogs occur' is a fair gloss.

claims.claim: Requires monthly summary statistics for each phone line, including caller satisfaction data.
claims.sourceSpan: a summary of the information described in paragraph (1) with respect to the prior month
claims.note: Caller satisfaction = 2(a)(4)(G).

claims.claim: Monthly metrics include average and median call lengths and hold times; percent disconnected or directed to automation; number transferred; and number/percent who indicated they received help.
claims.sourceSpan: the average and median amount of time that callers described in subparagraph (E) were on hold following the transfer, and
claims.note: Call lengths (A); hold time (F, specifically post-transfer hold); directed to automation (C); disconnected (D); transferred (E); received help (G).

claims.claim: The last metric requires the IRS to actively collect caller satisfaction data before calls end.
claims.sourceSpan: the number and percent of callers who indicated that they received the answers or service for which they were contacting the Internal Revenue Service.
claims.note: Bill requires reporting the number/percent who 'indicated' satisfaction; the specific mechanism 'actively collect ... before calls end' is a reasonable inference but is not stated in the text. Non-material.

claims.claim: Requires the Secretary, via website and mobile application, to give taxpayers individualized, up-to-date status on returns and amended returns: receipt, completed processing (with refund date and estimated receipt date), or suspension with reason and any requested information.
claims.sourceSpan: through a website and mobile application, the Secretary shall provide individualized, specific, and up-to-date information to taxpayers regarding their tax returns and amended returns
claims.note: Receipt 3(1); refund date 3(2)(A); estimated date 3(2)(B); suspension/reason 3(3)(A); requested info 3(3)(B).

claims.claim: Deadline: not later than January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 12 months after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 12 months after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: For electronic refunds, must show the partial/full account number plus the institution's name and routing number; for paper checks, the mailing address.
claims.sourceSpan: the name and routing number of the financial institution
claims.note: Partial/full account number 3(2)(C)(i)(I); paper-check address 3(2)(C)(ii).

claims.claim: Sense of Congress that taxpayers should be able to request a callback, and that by calendar year 2028 the IRS should offer a callback for any call to an applicable phone number extension not answered within 5 minutes.
claims.sourceSpan: taxpayers contacting the Internal Revenue Service should have the option to receive a callback, and
claims.note: CY2028 / 5-minute callback = 4(2).

claims.claim: Sense-of-Congress provision (non-binding); applies to any taxpayer, including those residing outside the United States.
claims.sourceSpan: any taxpayer (including any taxpayer residing outside of the United States) the option to receive a callback
claims.note: 'It is the sense of Congress that' = non-binding.

claims.claim: Requires the Secretary to make available a website or mobile application letting any taxpayer view returns, documents, notices and letters from the prior 6-year period, respond to IRS notices online, and authorize representatives, preparers, or qualified reporting agents to access them.
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary shall make available a website or mobile application which allows any taxpayer
claims.note: View 5(a)(1); prior 6-year period 5(d)(1); respond 5(a)(2); authorize reps/preparers/agents 5(a)(3).

claims.claim: Deadline: not later than January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 18 months after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall make available a website or mobile application

claims.claim: Consistent with section 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code.
claims.sourceSpan: in a manner consistent with any applicable limitations under section 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986

claims.claim: Also requires a program to investigate unauthorized access by designated persons, with annual public reporting.
claims.sourceSpan: annually publish, on the public website of the Internal Revenue Service, the actions undertaken
claims.note: Program to investigate = 5(f)(1); annual reporting = 5(f)(2).

claims.claim: Requires taxpayer/tax-professional focus groups before launch.
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary shall conduct focus groups with taxpayers and tax professionals
claims.note: 'prior to the date that the website or mobile application ... is made available' = before launch.

claims.claim: Requirement for real-time IRS public dashboard with per-phone-line call volume, wait times, and callback availability, plus public API access.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary shall require the Internal Revenue Service to provide in real time on its public website

claims.claim: Monthly IRS reporting requirement including caller satisfaction metrics, disconnection rates, and hold times per phone extension.
claims.sourceSpan: the number and percent of calls that were disconnected or terminated by the Internal Revenue Service,

claims.claim: Requirement for IRS to provide taxpayers with online or mobile access to returns, notices, refund status, and estimated refund date.
claims.sourceSpan: the estimated date on which the taxpayer can expect to receive such refund

claims.claim: Requirement for IRS to use technology to detect and screen automated calls.
claims.sourceSpan: use technology to detect and screen out automated calls

claims.claim: Monthly statistics include the number and percent of callers who indicated they received the answers or service they were seeking - a satisfaction data point embedded in a call-volume requirement.
claims.sourceSpan: the number and percent of callers who indicated that they received the answers or service for which they were contacting the Internal Revenue Service.

claims.claim: Collecting this metric requires the IRS to actively ask callers before they hang up whether their issue was resolved, effectively mandating a caller survey process.
claims.sourceSpan: the number and percent of callers who indicated that they received the answers or service for which they were contacting the Internal Revenue Service.
claims.note: The 'before they hang up' timing and 'survey process' framing are analytical inferences; the bill states only that the number/percent who 'indicated' satisfaction must be reported. Non-material synthesis.

claims.claim: The bill requires real-time call data but does not specify a minimum uptime requirement for the dashboard or what disclosures are required if the live data is unavailable.
claims.sourceSpan: to provide in real time on its public website, to the extent practical, the following:
claims.note: Bill hedges with 'to the extent practical' but sets no uptime/disclosure standard; the gap is an accurate absence claim.

claims.claim: The digital access requirement does not specify an implementation timeline for the mobile application option.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 12 months after the date of enactment of this Act, through a website and mobile application, the Secretary shall provide individualized, specific, and up-to-date information to taxpayers regarding their tax returns and amended returns
claims.note: The bill DOES specify implementation timelines that expressly cover the mobile application: Section 3 sets a 'not later than January 1 ... more than 12 months after enactment' deadline for the website AND mobile application, and Section 5(a) sets an 18-month deadline for the website or mobile application. Claiming no timeline exists misinforms the reader.

claims.claim: The digital access requirement does not specify minimum device or accessibility standards for the application.
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary shall make available a website or mobile application which allows any taxpayer
claims.note: No device/accessibility standards appear anywhere in the text; this portion of the gap is accurate.

claims.claim: The 'applicable phone number extension' definition includes a threshold of any line that received not less than 200,000 calls in the preceding calendar year (and specific IRS functions/contractor lines).
claims.sourceSpan: received not less than 200,000 calls during the preceding calendar year.
claims.note: Analysis glosses the defined term as 'phone line'/'public phone line' and omits the concrete scoping (functions + 200,000-call threshold). Minor definitional omission.

claims.claim: 'Significant delay' is defined as failure to process applicable items received at least 21 days before the first day of the week.
claims.sourceSpan: the failure to process all of such applicable items which were received by the Internal Revenue Service at least 21 days before the first day of the week.
claims.note: The 21-day threshold defining what triggers weekly delay reporting is not surfaced in the analysis. Minor definitional omission.

claims.claim: The website must embed an application/tool that estimates the approximate wait time to reach a representative.
claims.sourceSpan: estimates the approximate wait time to speak directly with a representative of the Internal Revenue Service.
claims.note: The embedded estimated-wait-time tool (2(a)(2)) is only loosely implied by 'wait times' in the summary. Minor omission.

notes: Source read in full (12,958 chars, no referencedSources registered on the analysis). Two material issues: (1) gaps[1] states the bill specifies no implementation timeline for the mobile app, but Section 3 sets a 12-month deadline covering the website AND mobile application (and Section 5 an 18-month deadline) - a direction/contradiction error. (2) top_lines[2] ('Monthly Accountability Metrics' + callback sense-of-Congress) is tagged billSection '3', but its content is Section 2(a)(4) and Section 4 - a wrong-account attribution; correct anchor is '2'. All substantive factual claims about the bill's provisions (figures 5 minutes, CY2028, 6-year period, 12/18-month deadlines, per-extension metrics, API, refund detail, online-accounts scope) verified verbatim against source. featured_quotes were not audited (Congressional Record source not available in this pass; the rubric handles CR quotes as kind:'quote' rows against CR text). billType 'amendment' not audited as a source-fidelity claim (editorial taxonomy).
